target_customer: Engineering and R&D teams at large manufacturers and life science firms that run simulations
problem: Engineers needed high performance computing for simulation but lacked on premise clusters. Rescale packaged cloud HPC with simulation software on demand.
business_model: Usage-based cloud HPC and software platform with enterprise contracts
product_category: Cloud HPC and engineering simulation platform

founders.name: Joris Poort
education: University of Michigan, mechanical engineering and mathematics
University of Washington, aeronautics and astronautics
founders.background_notes: Per VentureBeat 2021-02-02, both founders optimized the 787 wing structure at Boeing with AI techniques.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating HPC jobs, licensing and many simulation codes across cloud providers needed deep systems work with large data.

defensibility.rationale: Pre-installed application library and enterprise integration create switching costs, but cloud vendors could offer similar services.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large clouds did not displace it; Microsoft and Nvidia later invested in the 2021 Series C.

market_need_then: Engineering simulation needed scarce HPC capacity. The company says it began after Boeing was not interested in starting a cloud HPC business (secondary account).

branding.community_and_virality: Hosts the Big Compute podcast and conference series per its YC page and site.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in the HPC and engineering software niche, no brand-level press found.

outcome_analysis: Rescale was founded by two former Boeing aerospace engineers and grew into an enterprise cloud HPC platform with customers among large automakers and life science firms. It raised a 32M Series B in 2018 and a Series C of 50M in 2021 later reported as expanded to 105M. A 2025 Series D is reported by a secondary source. No exit was found.
notes: Series A of 14M in 2016 (TransLink) appears only in a secondary summary and is unverified, so not recorded. A 115M Series D in April 2025 is reported by one Dutch outlet and an aggregator, so not recorded as a round. The Series C was expanded to 105M per a press release listing seen only in search results. Earlier pre-Series B rounds not found; coverage is partial. No competitor with a source dated near 2012 was found.
